DRAFT FOR REVIEW

CONFIDENTIAL CASE BRIEF FOR LEGAL REVIEW

From: [SENDER NAME AND ADDRESS]
To: [RECIPIENT NAME AND ADDRESS]

Subject: Suspected forged contract (commercial/fraud)

MATERIAL FACTS

1. Bright Path Logistics, a small trucking firm, is being sued by Orion Traders for 18,00,000 for alleged breach of a supply and transport agreement dated 1 February. Bright Path's owner, Anil Chopra, says he never signed any such agreement. Orion's lawyer has submitted a 12-page contract that appears to bear Anil's signature, with an "effective date" of 1 March, which is after the signing date written on the last page. Anil says the signature is similar to his but "not exactly right."

2. Anil admits he had several email exchanges and a short meeting with Orion's representative in January about a possible trial arrangement, but says it never went beyond discussion. Orion says that Anil signed in person and that performance began when Bright Path moved three loads in March. Anil says the three loads were separate, paid one-off jobs. He wants to know whether the contract can be challenged as forged, how to prove it, and whether he risks being found liable even if the signature is disputed.

OUTCOME SOUGHT AND QUESTIONS FOR COUNSEL

[Specify the requested action or relief]

ENCLOSURES

None

Place: [place]
Date: [date of signing]
